applicable_when: The kernel runs only 128 blocks on 132 SMs (0.32 waves/SM), so most SMs are idle for most of the kernel lifetime. 168 registers/thread caps occupancy at 3 blocks/SM (18.75% theoretical) and achieved is only 6.25% — warp-level latency hiding is nearly absent. The B-matrix load uses a double broadcast_to pattern that causes 8-way shared memory bank conflicts on 69.89% of all shared loads (top NCU rule at 59.44% estimated speedup). On H200 (Hopper), TMA block pointers replace scalar pointer arithmetic with hardware-managed bulk async copies, eliminating the bank-conflict-prone manual indexing and enabling software pipelining via num_stages. Combined with @triton.autotune to explore smaller tiles (reduces register pressure) and larger num_stages (hides memory latency), this directly attacks all three top bottlenecks simultaneously.
